steps.name: Haggard Noble
steps.text: Name yourself, stranger.
...Fuze.

steps.name: Haggard Noble
steps.text: That accent... are you Ursine?

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: You could say that.

steps.name: Haggard Noble
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: The water tower is broken. I want to fix it.

steps.name: Haggard Noble
steps.text: Can't you fix it yourself? What does it have to do with me?

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: The problem is with the pump's Originium circuit. I understand engineering, and you know Originium Arts.

steps.name: Haggard Noble
steps.text: ...A well-armed, masked Ursine? Here to fix a water tower in a Leithanien town?

steps.name: Townsfolk
steps.text: Mr. Berman...

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Oh, it's you. What's with this man?

steps.name: Townsfolk
steps.text: Vissel and I were attacked by needleflies when fetching water from the river. Vissel got hurt, but we made it back alive thanks to Fuze here.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Vissel got hurt? Is it serious?

steps.name: Townsfolk
steps.text: He's still alive... that's all I can say. His granddaughter is by his side.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: I see. Go on.

steps.name: Townsfolk
steps.text: We invited him into town, and that's when he saw the broken water tower. He tried to fix it and found that the problem was with the Originium circuit, not the mechanical components...

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: I see.

steps.name: Townsfolk
steps.text: I-I'll be going.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: So you asked him if he knew anyone who knew Originium Arts, and he brought you to me.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: (Nods) I'm hoping you can help your subjects.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: I'm not their lord.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: He said the Baron built this water tower many years ago. I asked him where the Baron lived, and he brought me to you.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: You heard him call me Mr. Berman, not Baron.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Very well... Mr. Berman. This is a facility that makes people's lives better.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: People used to go to the river to fetch water all the time. They managed just fine.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Maybe it was the water tower's pumps that created a space for the needleflies to make their nest.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: All I know is that Vissel wouldn't be at death's door if the water tower was fixed earlier.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: What difference does one death make?

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: You think his death doesn't matter?

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: It's not just him.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Him, me, this whole town, all of Leithanien... all of it is irreversibly moving towards decay and death.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: The difference between needlefly and old age is no more than the difference between arriving at your destination by burdenbeast or by foot.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: ...Ridiculous.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Where are you going?

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: To find others.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: There's no one else in town who knows Originium circuits. Whoever brought you to me must have told you.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Then I'll research it.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Why are you so stubborn about this? Over a bunch of people whom you've just met?

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: It's not about who, but what. Goodbye.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Wait.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: I have a few books on this topic that I bought when I was young.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: You spent a lot of time looking for them.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: It's not an easy thing, looking for books.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: 'Originium Circuit Theory and Applications', from Victoria. Wasn't easy to find a book that wasn't in Leithanian at home.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: You must have question marks written all over your face behind that mask, Ursine. You don't know why I refuse to fix the water tower, but allow you to borrow my books.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: I have a theory.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Which is?

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: You want to prove that fixing the water tower won't change anything.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: It's not that complicated. I'm just curious.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: I thought you had completely lost interest.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Even a rock would be curious about why a heavily-armed foreigner wants to fix a water tower for your neighbor.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Either I fix it or I don't. That's all there is to it.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: No... what I'm curious is what this person has experienced, which has made him so stubborn about something that shouldn't have anything to do with him.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Would you like to stay over for the night, Mr. Fuze? Perhaps we can have a chat over dinner.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Thank you for the invitation, but I doubt we have much to talk about.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: I suppose you're right.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: ...But I would still have liked to have a chat.
Shuhrat— What is it?

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Sorry. Got lost in thought.
Fuze looks around him.
It is the corridor of Rhodes Island. He would not call it familiar, but it is not unknown to him either.
He has his hands around the back of his head, leaning against the wall outside Elias Kötz's quarters at Rhodes Island, waiting for 'Blitz' to come out.

steps.name: Blitz?
steps.text: It'll be a little longer. I haven't gotten used to Rhodes Island razors yet.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: That's fine, Kötz.

steps.name: Blitz?
steps.text: Where were we? Oh, the festival we saw at Leithanien.

steps.name: Blitz?
steps.text: There were a thousand casters at the festival. They stood silently like statues on the plaza before the opening ceremony.

steps.name: Blitz?
steps.text: They were waiting for a single note from the concertmaster. The cue for them to raise their Arts Units in unison was so quiet it was almost inaudible ...

steps.name: Blitz?
steps.text: Come on. A reaction would be nice, you know.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: It's hard for me to imagine it. Leithanian is too different from anything that I know. Imagine, one thousand robed, masked figures holding wands, standing on Registan Square...

steps.name: Blitz?
steps.text: Registan Square?

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: The landmark of Samarkand. You should know.

steps.name: Blitz?
steps.text: I see. I'll continue.

steps.name: Blitz?
steps.text: One thousand beams of Arts light shoot into the night sky. Colors clashed in the clouds and burst open, turning the entire sky into a colorful sea of flowers...

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Application of evocation-conversion Originium Arts?

steps.name: Blitz?
steps.text: You know Originium Arts?

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: The result of extra lessons in Dossoles.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Coal, oil, gas, even nuclear fusion... it's all been replaced by Originium. I had to learn from scratch—

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Blitz?
steps.text: Something wrong with the razor. One moment—
Fuze wakes with a start. He had fallen asleep on the desk, his faced buried in the book he was reading.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Tsk... my back hurts. And my head's groggy...

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: 'Festive scene witnessed by the author while visiting Leithanien...'

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: No wonder I was dreaming about it.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Something fell out... a bookmark?

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: I should return this with the book.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Press the switch there for me, please.

steps.name: Townsfolk
steps.text: Not working.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Looks like we need a few more books from Berman. Could you fetch them for me?

steps.name: Townsfolk
steps.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Fuze. Mr. Berman...

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: What about him? Don't tell me he does illegal stuff in secret. You were really nervous the first time I visited him.

steps.name: Townsfolk
steps.text: No, not at all! He's not a bad person. It's just... well... we don't go there unless we really need to.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: ...Fine, I'll go myself.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Let me see... 'Practical Manual of Home Appliances'? Isn't that a little too simple?

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Just because it's simple doesn't mean it can't help. I'll take this one.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: I'm curious, though... why would there be an Ursine who knows machines, but not Originium circuits?

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: That's not important right now.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Why don't we set the water tower aside for a moment and talk about our own lives?

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: There's no need for that.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Well, I'll start if you don't want to... starting with that water tower.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: The water tower was the first step of the Baron's dream. He wanted to help the people here live better lives. He hoped this place could be a 'model town.'

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: In the end, the only thing he achieved was tap water for the townsfolk.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: The Baron wanted to build a factory in town, get investments from bigwigs from the capital, make this place a center for the arts... but all his efforts ended up futile or unnoticed.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: His final attempt was the boldest, and it came closest to success. He wanted to move the entire town to a mobile platform. He had an agreement with a Vedunien factory, and paid a large amount up front—

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Then, Their Majesties visited their faithful Zwillingstürme.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Is that your story?

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: ...My father's.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: I was young then, still working on my university thesis about telepathic and perceptive Arts in Vedunien.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: At the end of it all, the only thing I could remember is blood. Blood of the common folk, of nobles, of the Gendarmerie, of the Kurfürsten, and of my teacher.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: I barely escaped with my life, clutching the charred thesis. The first thing my father asked when I came back was how I was doing. The second thing he asked was how the factory was doing... I need not tell you the answer.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Your father died a broken man, and you never inherited his title.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: I gave it up, because I realized it was all meaningless.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: ...Do you know what the biggest difference between you and your father is?

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: I'm all ears.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: He at least managed to give the townspeople tap water.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: If we talk about the issue at hand, your neighbors will have running water from tubes again tomorrow.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Then let's assume your work here will be done. You'll leave, not pausing for a moment.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: I'm sure there are many people as stubborn as I am in Leithanien. You can see for yourself.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: No. I only learned this recently. You're one of a kind.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: One of a kind?

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: It's nothing. I wish you luck in your studies.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: And if you see Vissel's granddaughter, tell her to bring him over before it's too late.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: 'Bring him over'? What do you mean?

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Exactly that.
This looks like a good place.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: It's really dark here.

steps.name: Doc?
steps.text: Looks like it's going to be a long time before we can go back to that place where everything doesn't run on Originium.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: I didn't know you were the kind to get homesick.

steps.name: Doc?
steps.text: Of course. You remember the day we first came?

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: I remember. We were investigating the Magnethill No.2 site and ended up landing on Reynell's golf balls.

steps.name: Doc?
steps.text: Speaking of home, what was the name of that landmark in Samarkand... Registan Square？

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Yeah. The building with the blue dome. I can almost see the crowds on the square, the cars driving by, and the patterns on the three buildings…
Fuze looks up from his book.
Sleep seems to come to him anytime, anywhere now. He often falls asleep halfway through a draft, and has to chase the remnants of the dream out of his mind after waking up.
The dreams were too clear, too real.
Sometimes, he even wonders if Terra was just a really, really long dream after he hit his head at Magnethill No. 2.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: (Yawns)

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: I can't sleep now. I need to go to the water tower... or borrow another book from Berman...

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: What did he say about Vissel's granddaughter? Tell her to bring him over?

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Thank you for bringing Vissel over while he still draws breath. Where's his granddaughter?

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: In bed. She's exhausted.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Why do you have the townspeople send the dying to you?

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: I asked around. People were hesitant at first, but they eventually told me that you've been doing this for a long time.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Let me guess... you suspect I'm taking advantage of the dead?

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: I am a bit skeptical, assuming what you told me is true.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: It's hard to believe someone so melancholy could be that bad. Especially when they can't put in the effort to do anything.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: ...Now you've offended me, Mr. Fuze. But that's fine.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: You haven't answered my question.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Then watch. You'll understand.
The sleepiness strikes again. Fuze bites on his tongue to prevent himself from falling asleep.
Berman gazes down at the old man's clouded eyes, and places one end of his staff on the old man's forehead.
The tip of the staff begins to glow.

steps.name: Vissel
steps.text: (Mumbled muttering)

steps.name: Vissel
steps.text: Levine, it's you... you came back... you really came back...

steps.name: Vissel
steps.text: No, don't apologize, no need to say anything... we'll go home.

steps.name: Vissel
steps.text: Here, an apple from the backyard... you wanted one when you left, but there wasn't any on the trees that year. I saved this one for you...
There is no apple on the old man's hand. Berman is the only person standing before him.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Who's Levine?

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Vissel's only son. He left the town more than a decade ago, after contracting Oripathy.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: What did you do to Vissel? Is he hallucinating?

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Of course not. That's beyond my reach.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: All I can do is alleviate their pain, help them relax, cause them to dream when it's neither the time nor place to do so... a midday dream that I cannot interfere with.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Sounds like a doctor administrating anesthetics to a patient in pain, except there's no syringe.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: If that's how you understand it, it's not my place to say any more.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Drug abuse ruins lives.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Is it abuse to let a dying person leave in peace? Shuhrat—

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: This is the most meaningful thing that I can do for someone, Mr. Fuze.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Perhaps Vissel wouldn't be dying if you had done something about the water tower earlier.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: You're the one drowning yourself in 'medicine' instead of helping the dying.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Ha, me?

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: I've seen too many tragedies. The more I see of them, the more I'm convinced that I'm right.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Catastrophe, intrigue, war, Originium, even minor accidents... the life and will of man is ever fragile before them, like dust in the wind.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: And soon I'll be gone with the wind too.
Berman unbuttons his shirt and reveals the Originium crystal formations in his abdomen.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: On the way back from Zwillingstürme, I found that I had a little black rock by the side of my ribs, one last parting gift from Vedunien.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: It has almost consumed me, and so I decided to commit a crime for the first and last time in my life.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Crime?

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: There is a lot of complicated preparation to be done in order for my Arts to work on a healthy and uncooperative mind. I'm sorry for doing this to you.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: It began as curiosity about what this quiet man of action talks about in his sleep, so I did something to the book and bookmark that I lent you.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Then, I heard you talk in your dream, about something beyond my wildest imagination... a blue sky, sky without a single trace of Originium.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: I don't expect to go with you to that place without Originium. I don't even expect to become friends with you. After all, you don't like people who don't talk about practical things, do you?

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: And so, I must use my Arts... so that we can finish this last midday dream together.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: I'm sorry to make you stay with a dying patient in his final moments, but he has been alone for too long.
Berman points his wand at Fuze before he could react.
Fuze is overcome by sleepiness.
He hears the flows of an undercurrent, pulling his drifting consciousness below the surface.
Shuhrat! Wake up!

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: *Cough,* *cough*...
Good, you're awake. Lucky for you, you saved yourself a bit of pain. Grab your gear. We're leaving.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Where are we?

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Magnethill No.2. The tremors have passed. You seem to have hit your head.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: There's nothing unusual in the labs. Doc and the others have already left. Investigation into any possible connections to Levi will have to wait until next time.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Mm... hm.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Do you have any vacation plans?

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Vacation?

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: You forgot that too? You really did hit your head hard, didn't you?

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: I need some help picking out a good place to relax.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: How about Samarkand? I hear Registan Square is beautiful.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: A place where I can lie down for a whole day, thinking about nothing.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Sure.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: But... wait... there's something I still need to do...

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: I don't know, but... Originium...

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: Originium? What's that? Did you have a dream while you were out cold?

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: I mean... have you ever heard of Originium?

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: You can't expect other people to understand what happens in your dreams.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Sorry... it's just that the word left an impression on me.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: There's no point in dwelling on it. It's better to just focus on Registan Square. You should come with me.

steps.name: Ela?
steps.text: Your cas— I mean, scientists, the best ones—

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: No, it's nothing.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: I'm just happy that I'm visiting your homeland.

steps.name: Ela
steps.text: A place with no catastrophe, no war, no tragedies.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: No... tragedies?

steps.name: Ela?
steps.text: Shuhrat? What is it?

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Do you remember Oregon?

steps.name: Ela?
steps.text: Shuhrat—

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Tell me, what do you think of Oregon?

steps.name: Ela?
steps.text: O-Oregon? A good place for artists, with nice museums, orchestras...

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: What about Baghdad? Lebanon? Moscow?

steps.name: Ela?
steps.text: Shuhrat, listen...

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Did you think that without Originium—

steps.name: Ela?
steps.text: No, no!

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: —Without Originium, there won't be any tragedies, Berman?

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: (Forced smile) Of course not, Shuhrat.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Perhaps it would all happen again, absent Originium. But don't be so hard on a dying patient's dream.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Maybe you should go and see the places that I talked about. See what happened to my home without Originium.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: There's no need. I take it that no less blood was spilled there than Vedunien that autumn.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: It's not the amount of bloodshed that matters.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Ha... you're one to talk now, Shuhrat.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Go.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: The Arts have failed. You can no longer tell me what it looks like beneath that blue sky, nor can I experience it again through your narration.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Go, before I turn to a pile of dust. Bring my first and final crime to a painless end.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: What is it? You wanted to talk to a man who achieved nothing?

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Perhaps there are less tragedies in this world... these lands... than you think.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Then what did I see in Vedunien? What did you see in the places that you talked about?

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Chaos.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Chaos is just that. Sometimes it brings destruction and other times, it guides you through it.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Chaos doesn't always end in tragedy, unless...

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Unless no one takes action?

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Perhaps, Shuhrat. But it's too late.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Too late.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Does the soul linger after death?

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: I know little about this topic.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: It's fine. I'm just thinking... if it does, do you think my soul can visit the Samarkand of your memories, and see the blue dome above?

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: If you wish...

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: ...I'm not opposed to telling you how it looks, of my own volition.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Am I still worthy to hear it?

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: Don't leave this world without achieving anything.
The haggard man's eyes go wide, then he laughs feebly.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Perhaps the reason that you don't like to talk is you're too smart. Smart people are good at offending others.
Fuze shrugs and begins to describe the plaza and the nearby buildings, in as much detail as possible.
Berman raises his wand, and a lifelike model of Registan Square begins to form before the desk.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: ...Looks just like it. Almost identical.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Good to hear.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Where will you go?

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: The water tower. I'll stay in town a little longer, finish what you could not.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: Go. Take Vissel home. Let him spend his last moments with his granddaughter.

steps.name: Fuze
steps.text: I will. Goodbye.

steps.name: Berman
steps.text: ...Take care.
As the door locks behind Fuze, Berman raises his wand with what little strength he has left.
There is no music, only the sound of doors and windows sealing.
The wand falls to the ground, but Berman could no longer hear it. He feels the blue dome of the model, imagining the sky of the same color, the sky he hasn't, and won't be able to see.
